items.stem: Why are frequent large temporary objects (over the LOH threshold) a performance concern?

options.text: They land on the Large Object Heap and trigger expensive Gen 2 collections
options.rationale: Correct: large objects go to the LOH and cause costly Gen 2 work.

options.text: They are stored on the stack and overflow it
options.rationale: Large objects are heap-allocated, not stack-allocated.

options.text: They are never collected at all
options.rationale: They are collected, but in expensive Gen 2 collections.
They do not disable the GC.

items.explanation: Correct: large objects go to the LOH and cause costly Gen 2 work.

items.stem: Which TWO are correct about resource lifetime in .NET? (Select TWO.)

options.text: HttpClient should be reused rather than created and disposed per call
options.rationale: Correct: creating an HttpClient per call can exhaust sockets.

options.text: Objects implementing IDisposable should be disposed, e.g. with using
options.rationale: Correct: disposing releases unmanaged or scarce resources promptly.

options.text: GC.Collect should be called on every request
options.rationale: Forcing collections in production hurts performance.

options.text: Finalizers are the preferred way to release resources deterministically
options.rationale: Dispose is deterministic; finalizers are not.

items.explanation: Correct: creating an HttpClient per call can exhaust sockets.

items.stem: Task Manager shows a high working set for a .NET process. What does that tell you about the managed heap?

options.text: Not much directly; working set is not the same as managed-heap usage
options.rationale: Correct: working set includes more than the managed heap, so measure the heap specifically.

options.text: The managed heap is exactly that size
options.rationale: Working set is not a direct measure of the managed heap.

options.text: There is definitely a managed memory leak
options.rationale: High working set alone does not prove a managed leak.
A high working set does not mean the GC stopped.

items.explanation: Correct: working set includes more than the managed heap, so measure the heap specifically.
